A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original experiments and supplementary analyses can be matched despite renumbering and additions.

before.justification: V1 reports original Llama and Mamba training experiments and loss-to-loss scaling analyses across model checkpoints, including intervention results in the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original training and scaling experiments and additionally reports numerical model comparisons and quantified intervention effects.

M1.justification: The model architectures, training objectives, intervention framework, and central shifted-power-law fitting approach are retained. Appendix B provides additional fitting documentation without establishing that the underlying procedure changed; BPB normalization changes evaluation.

E1.justification: OpenBookQA is removed from the reported task list and corresponding appendix scaling plots. The pretraining and validation corpora and remaining nine downstream tasks are retained. COPA appears in v2 Figure 2 but was already evaluated in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the GPT, Llama, Mamba, and Mamba2 architecture groups and the same tokenizer alternatives. The new point-wise comparison uses the existing Llama–Mamba pairing; the pretrained-model inventory adds identification details rather than establishing new comparators.

E3.justification: Cross-tokenizer evaluation changes from token-based loss to byte-normalized BPB, materially changing the basis of a central comparison. V2 also reports few-step Llama-7B checkpoints, point-wise comparisons after approximately eight billion tokens, and a new curve-area metric evaluated over [0, 2].

E4.justification: V2 supplements the retained intervention suite with matched-loss architecture comparisons in Section 5/Table 1, quantitative curve-separation analysis in Appendix D/Table 4, and a larger-model check in Figure 1. Existing alternative-axis and individual-task analyses remain in the appendices.

E5.justification: Figure 1 newly reports R-squared goodness-of-fit values of 0.998–0.999. The existing statements about 200–800 checkpoints and varying seeds remain; no increase in independent runs or new confidence intervals is documented.

E6.justification: BPB-based results replace the moderate tokenizer-effect finding with generally minor differences; these are not same-metric performance gains. Figure 4 and Section 4.1 change the Pile/deduplicated-Pile finding from coincident to separated curves. New tables add concrete results, including base-to-data and base-to-tokenizer curve areas of 0.22 and 0.01; OpenBookQA results disappear.

T1.justification: Appendices A–B add explicit mathematical specifications for compute-to-loss fitting, including the minimum-observed-loss fallback estimator in Equation 5, which v1 did not specify. The central shifted-power-law equation and irreducible-error interpretation remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, main observations, and conclusion move tokenizer choice from a dominant determinant alongside pretraining data to a generally minor or negligible factor. V2 also foregrounds the implication that similar training losses on the same data yield closely matched downstream performance across training setups.

C2.justification: V1 attributes tokenizer differences to special-token handling and interprets deduplication as preserving the data distribution. V2 instead proposes weight tying as an untested explanation for exceptional pretrained-model curves and interprets deduplication as meaningfully changing the distribution. These revise substantive explanations of central findings.

D1.justification: V2 specifies SciPy curve_fit and fallback estimation, lists pretrained model names, sizes, datasets, and tokenizers, and clarifies tokenizer-ablation details in Tables 2–3. Conversely, v1's code-website statement and link are removed; this establishes lost access guidance, not that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: V2 adds the SciPy reference and removes the OpenBookQA reference. It also drops v1's novelty assertion about special-token effects. The main positioning relative to loss-to-loss scaling and robustness research remains intact; the OLMo publication update identifies the same work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized revisions to the abstract, introduction, tokenizer discussion, and conclusion, adds a short Point-wise Comparisons section, and expands appendix explanations. Most of the original prose and narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds three tables and a compute-to-loss contour figure, redraws the central tokenizer plots and appendix counterparts with BPB axes, and adds fit annotations and highlighted checkpoints to Figure 1. It also corrects several model-size, context-length, and optimizer captions in the final appendix figures.

improvement.justification: BPB normalization addresses a central cross-tokenizer comparability problem underlying v1's headline conclusion, and v2 revises that conclusion while acknowledging exceptional models. Numerical intervention comparisons and clearer fitting documentation make the evidence substantially easier to assess. Removing the code-access link is a drawback, but the correction to this central scientific comparison outweighs it.
